description.purpose: A GET a manifest can name: one web_fetch cell as a whole template, so a running colony can be given the ability to read a document off the network by a declaration instead of by a hand-built subtree. It fetches what it is ASKED for -- the URL rides in the tool_call args, not in this config.
description.use_when: Wherever a colony has to read something over HTTP: a feed, an API endpoint, a page. Instantiate it under a name that says what it fetches, and draw both edges in the same mutation -- one in from whoever composes the tool_call, one out to whoever reads the answer.
description.not_in_scope: GET only; method, request headers and a request body are a core roadmap defer of the cell type and cannot be shipped by a template. No retries, no caching, no parsing of the answer, and no URL of its own -- a fetcher with a target baked in would be a fetcher for one caller.
description.emits_meaning: messages[]: one tool_result turn whose text is the response body, truncated visibly at max_bytes. hop.operation is always 'web_fetch'; hop.http_status carries the answer's status, and a non-2xx is a NORMAL result an edge decides about; error_code is set only for io_error, timeout, invalid_input, target_blocked, too_many_redirects and invalid_redirect.
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: a tool_call turn whose text is the JSON args {url}. A missing, non-string, empty, syntactically broken or non-http(s) URL is invalid_input, and the answer quotes the URL back.
examples: {"url": "https://example.com/feed.xml"} -> tool_result with the document, hop { operation: 'web_fetch', http_status: 200, bytes: 4211 }
a 404 -> the same shape with hop.http_status 404 and no error_code: the edge decides, the cell reports
{"url": "http://169.254.169.254/"} -> error_code 'target_blocked' -- link-local stays shut in BOTH steps of the opt-out
